newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed on uncertainties.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Friday with investors seen liquidating their positions ahead of the return of Hong Kong to China on July 1 and amid uncertainties about short-term market trend, traders said.
The key November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,303 yuan ($398) per tonne, rising 15 yuan. It opened at 3,290 yuan and hit a low of 3,286 yuan per tonne.
July rose 95 yuan to 3,355, September fell 58 to 3,200, the January 1998 contract two to 3,334 and March four to 3,296.
Combined volume rose to 28,000 tonnnes from 26,800 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mixed and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Retail investors dominated today's trading with many investors eager to liquidate their positions before the holiday," one trader said.
The exchange will close on Monday and Tuesday to mark the return of Hong Kong, exchange officials said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the short term in the absence of market-moving news.
